name: k_hop_neighborhood
description: Finds every node within k hops (steps along edges) of a given node, using breadth-first search. Use for questions like 'who is within two hops of Alice?', 'which airports can I reach from Chennai with at most one change?' (k=2) or 'which courses lead to this one?' (direction 'in'). Works on directed and undirected graphs, weighted or not (weights are ignored; only the number of hops counts). Returns how many nodes were found, how many sit at each hop distance, and the nearest top_k nodes with their hop distance. Also registers the neighbourhood (the start node plus all nodes found) as a new graph and returns its id in result_graph_id, so other tools can run on it. Needs a node id: use lookup_node first to turn a name into an id.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

node.description: Id of the start node, e.g. 'MAA' in airports or 'm1' in karate. Use lookup_node to find it from a name.

k.description: Maximum number of hops from the start node. k=1 gives direct neighbours.

direction.description: Directed graphs only: 'out' follows edges forwards (where can I get to), 'in' follows them backwards (who can get here), 'both' ignores direction. Ignored on undirected graphs.

top_k.description: How many of the found nodes to list, nearest first. The counts always cover all of them.
